steps.title: Into the glomerulus
steps.say: Blood enters the glomerulus through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole. Watch the tuft: this is where plasma is filtered out into Bowman's capsule.

steps.title: Net filtration pressure
steps.say: The pressure pushing fluid out of the glomerular capillaries is about 55 millimetres of mercury. Bowman's capsule pushes back with about 15, and plasma oncotic pressure pulls back with about 30, so the net filtration pressure is about 10. That gives a GFR of about 125 millilitres a minute, or 180 litres a day.

steps.title: Afferent vs efferent
steps.say: Your note adds a control point. Constricting the efferent arteriole raises glomerular pressure and GFR, while constricting the afferent arteriole lowers both. This plate keeps both arterioles fixed, so take this one in words.

steps.title: Proximal tubule
steps.say: In the proximal convoluted tubule, about 65 percent of the filtered sodium and water is reabsorbed, with all the glucose and amino acids and about 80 percent of the bicarbonate. Because water follows the salt, reabsorption is iso-osmotic: the fluid stays at about 300 milliosmoles per kilogram.

steps.title: Thin descending limb
steps.say: The thin descending limb is permeable to water but not to salt. As it dives into the medulla, water leaves, so the fluid concentrates to about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram at the tip of the loop.

steps.title: Thick ascending limb
steps.say: The thick ascending limb is impermeable to water, and it actively pumps out sodium, potassium and chloride through NKCC2. So the fluid is diluted to about 100, which is why it is called the diluting segment. That pumping builds the medullary osmotic gradient from 300 to 1200, and furosemide works by blocking NKCC2.

steps.title: Distal tubule
steps.say: In the distal convoluted tubule, sodium and chloride are reabsorbed. This is the thiazide-sensitive step.

steps.title: Aldosterone
steps.say: Aldosterone acts on the principal cells, increasing sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion.

steps.title: ADH and concentrated urine
steps.say: ADH, also called vasopressin, inserts aquaporin 2 into the collecting duct. Water then moves out into the hypertonic medulla, giving concentrated urine of up to about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram. Without ADH the urine stays dilute, about 50 to 100.

steps.title: Key numbers
steps.say: So only about 1 to 2 litres of urine leave each day, which means more than 99 percent of the filtrate is reabsorbed.
